KKL Chairman Eyal Ostrovsky responds to the controversy surrounding the Jewish shepherds near Majd al-Krum.

From his remarks:

1. Grazing in the area is essential for preventing fires by reducing vegetation, and therefore it will continue.

2. Although grazing is necessary and was duly approved, mistakes and failures occurred in its implementation. We take responsibility for these mistakes and failures and will correct them.

3. At this stage, and at this stage only, for the coming days and until after Yom Kippur, the shepherds' encampment, which was set up because it was established largely not on KKL lands, has been dismantled.
This encampment included more tents than permitted and, in our view, more people than necessary.

4. Immediately after Yom Kippur, grazing will resume. The encampment's location will be set on KKL lands and moved away from the residential area and the blue line of Majd al-Krum.
The number of people staying in the encampment will be reduced from five to a maximum of three, the size of the residential encampment will be reduced, and the infrastructure and equipment present will be minimal and include only what is essential for maintaining the herd and nothing more.

##

In other words, and unofficially: KKL erred in the location of the encampment it approved for the Jewish shepherds. After Yom Kippur, it will allow the establishment of a new, smaller encampment in a nearby area so that sheep grazing can continue.

"The Great Evacuation Operation in Honor of Yuval Avraham and Rachel Shor"

I suppose not all of you know, but NZA is not Rachel Shor and Yuval Avraham’s first film.

Both of them, together with the Palestinian Basel Adra, produced in recent years the film "No Other Land," which documents Adra as he opposes the evacuation of his (squatting) family from the area of South Mount Hebron, known to Palestinians as "Masafer Yatta"—and also called, for our purposes, "Firing Zone 918."

The Palestinian-Norwegian film premiered at the Berlin International Film Festival in February 2024 to promote the Palestinian (false—sources to follow) narrative regarding Palestinian possession of this land.

So why is this interesting now, and in general?

In March 2022, the High Court of Justice, with a majority of liberal justices (Yitzhak Amit, Ofer Grosskopf, and David Mintz), ruled that Adra’s family—the subject of Yuval Avraham and Rachel Shor’s film—and the other Palestinian families residing in "Firing Zone 918"/"Masafer Yatta" are there illegally and must be evacuated.

(Trivia: Palestinians call the place "Masafer Yatta" to create an association between Firing Zone 918 and the village of Yatta in the Hebron district—out of thin air).

I should note that there was no Palestinian presence on the land, and it served as an air force firing zone as far back as 1990—there were no structures there. This was proven beyond any doubt based on satellite images provided by the Regavim organization.
The High Court, with a liberal panel, dismissed the petitioners (the Adra family and the other families) outright.

Four and a half years have passed since then, and out of about 700 illegal structures, only a few dozen have been evacuated—in other words, over 600 illegal structures still stand and serve as fertile ground for pro-Palestinian organizations to produce anti-Israeli narrative videos, with "humanitarian ambushes" for IDF soldiers—while they remain in a firing zone where entry is prohibited.

Attached is an up-to-date map marking the illegal structures that have not yet been evacuated (in green) and the houses that have been demolished (in red).
The High Court ruling is also attached.
Also attached is documentation of Yuval Avraham in Firing Zone 918 during the filming of "No Other Land."

What do I propose?

I propose to start tomorrow morning with an unprecedented evacuation operation to remove the 600 illegal structures, according to the High Court’s decision, and to call it "The Evacuation Operation in Honor of Yuval Avraham and Rachel Shor."
That way, the two will feel they really made a difference. But for the better... implementing the High Court’s ruling.

It’s unclear what the Israeli authorities are waiting for—but here is a rare window of opportunity.

Let’s get evacuating!!!! The excuses are over.
